items.caption: What the tile shows: PV generation and consumption as forecast curves (P50) with an uncertainty band (P10–P90) for up to 5 days — the EMS view: generation against consumption, the gap is grid import/export. Hover/touch shows the values and the balance at that time of day.

Sources: the PV and load forecast instances are found automatically (choose manually only if there are several instances). The tile also works with just one source; every series can be hidden with its switch or by clicking its legend entry.

Actual values: with the two actual-power variables, the current value appears in the legend, a dot on the now line, the measured course of the day as a dashed line (optional) and the actual kWh below the forecast values. The unit W/kW is detected automatically.

✨ Detail (outlier protection, 01.09.2026): a single defective archive value (e.g. a communication error in a partner module in the order of megawatts) is now discarded instead of distorting the “actual” comparison with the forecast - a generic implausibility limit (1 MW), not a plant-specific value.
Yesterday: shows the previous day with the measured curve (whole day) and the forecast made at that time. This shows how well the forecast hit the mark.

Chart engine: ECharts (open source, free of charge for commercial use too) or Highcharts (free for private/non-commercial use only). Both look practically the same; the library is loaded from a CDN (the display device needs internet access). Switch it in the expanded tile view (double arrow), not here in the form.

Appearance: line width, smoothing, band transparency, grid, y-axis, colors, font/size, days, actual display, cache — all adjustable in the expanded tile view (double arrow), not here in the form. The archive cache (actual course) reduces the load; the default of 120 s is enough.
Tip: pull the tile large enough in the WebFront (tile size = visible area, the chart height adapts automatically).

items.name: HookInfo
items.caption: IPSView/popup: the tile also runs as a standalone web page at http://<Symcon-IP>:3777%s (auto-refresh every 30 s). In IPSView, place a WebView element on a popup page and enter this URL. Note: WebHooks can be reached on the local network without logging in.

items.name: StandaloneEnabled
items.caption: Enable standalone web page for browser and IPSView

Only needed if the tile is to run as its own web page (browser, IPSView). If you only use the tile in the WebFront, you can switch this off: then no WebHook is registered and access from outside is removed. Switching it off removes the existing entry.

✨ Detail (start the tour yourself at any time, 01.09.2026): a clearly visible “?” button at the bottom left of the tile shows the introduction tour again at any time - regardless of the saved “already seen” status. Intended for shared instances (e.g. a demo/showcase instance with one shared login for all visitors).
